role.altitude: The environmental engineer keeps scoping projects, evaluating work, judging what rules mean for a client and directing fieldwork; chasing status in spreadsheets, searching regulations, tracking permit dates and downloading logger files shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting data checks on monitoring feeds and keeping the regulation library current
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who sees a monitoring gap the day it starts and never misses a permit review date.

tasks.short: Plan environmental protection programs or projects with the client, assign work to staff and contractors, track progress and budget, evaluate work delivered and report status to management and the client.

steps.what: Environmental engineer plans the project scope and work packages with the client
Environmental engineer assigns work to team members and contractors: by mail with the scope retyped today; after the change by picking people on the work packages already in the project system
Environmental engineer checks the final assignments: each package's scope, person or contractor, dates and budget match the plan
Environmental engineer releases the checked assignments to team members and contractors in the project system
Team members log their hours and report task status: by status mail today, by setting the status on their work package in the project system after the change
Environmental engineer tracks progress, hours and budget from spreadsheets and status mails
Environmental engineer evaluates work delivered by the team and contractors
Environmental engineer prepares the status report on progress, hours and budget: merged from spreadsheets and mails today, read from the dashboard with the engineer's comments after the change
Environmental engineer reports status to management and the client in progress meetings

tasks.design: Work packages and assignments live in a project system instead of spreadsheets and mail. Team members log hours against packages and set task status there, and contractors' invoices are booked against the same packages, so a dashboard shows progress, hours and budget per package. The engineer prepares progress meetings from the dashboard. Scoping and evaluating work stay with the engineer. The dashboard shows packages, not individual performance.

approvals.approved_version: The work package assignments with scope, assignee, dates and budget exactly as checked by the engineer in s2b, released once in the project system to the named team members and contractors; any change needs a new check and release.

tasks.previous_blocker: Status lived in mails and personal spreadsheets that had to be merged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Project systems with timesheets and budget dashboards.
tasks.still_hard: Projects whose scope shifts when contamination turns out larger.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a contractor's work is good enough.
tasks.altitude: Less chasing status; managing and judging stay.

evidence.claim: Recurring status reports can become a dashboard over project records.
Systems that check staff performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: running one project from plan to status reports; acquisition is outside.

Input contract for s3: hours logged weekly by team members against work packages, task status set by them (s3a, replacing their status mails), and contractor invoices booked by finance against packages; about 80% of projects run fully in the project system; s3 and the status report preparation (s5) are priced at that share.
Planning, evaluating and the progress meetings keep their full time. Assigning keeps 90 because the scope is no longer retyped into mails; checking and releasing assignments keep their full time.
unknowns: How many projects each engineer runs at once.

incremental.description: Environmental engineer keeps work packages current when scope changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of projects run fully in the project system, so tracking (s3) keeps 66 and status preparation (s5) keeps 63 (11.2); high: about 80% of projects in the system as assumed (17.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clarify the client's question, research environmental policies and standards that apply, analyse the client's situation, write the advice, have it reviewed and send it to industries or government agencies.

steps.what: Environmental engineer clarifies the question with the industry or government client
Environmental engineer researches the environmental policies and standards that apply

loop.input: The defined question and the firm's library of EU, national and provincial regulations and standards.
loop.output: A list of articles and standards that may apply, each with a quote and link.
loop.check: Every item must quote a document in the library, and the quote must state the obligation the item claims with its scope (activity, threshold, region, date in force), or the item is flagged; items whose fit to the client's case is unclear go to the engineer; the engineer opens each cited article before relying on it.
loop.stop: One list per question; the engineer adds what is missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses rules that use other terms for the same activity.

steps.what: Environmental engineer analyses the client's situation against the policies and standards
Environmental engineer writes the advice memo
Senior engineer reviews the final advice memo against the analysis and the client's question, checks the addressee, and approves it
Environmental engineer sends the approved advice to the client

approvals.approved_version: The advice memo exactly as approved by the senior engineer in s5, sent once by e-mail to the client contact who asked the question; any change goes back for a new approval.

tasks.design: A search step over the firm's own library of regulations and standards lists articles that may apply, each with a quote and link, and the engineer opens every one. Analysing the client's case and the advice itself stay with the engineer; the memo uses a template with standard sections. A senior engineer approves before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules were found by memory and keyword searches across many sources.
tasks.enabler_now: Search with quotes over a curated library of regulations.
tasks.still_hard: Rules that conflict or are being revised.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how the authority actually applies a rule.
tasks.altitude: Less searching; advice stays the engineer's.

evidence.claim: In a writing experiment with 453 professionals (no engineers), time fell 40% and quality rose 18%.
An answer desk with citations can serve literature and rule look-ups.

assumptions: Boundary: one advice question from intake to sending; follow-up talks are outside.
Input contract for s2: a library of regulations and standards kept current by the firm's knowledge team.
Analysis keeps its full time; the senior engineer's time is outside the engineer's savings.
unknowns: How complete the regulation library is.
research_questions: Does the search find rules the engineer would have missed?

already_counted.description: Environmental engineer opens and checks each cited article.

incremental.description: Environmental engineer reports missing or outdated documents to the knowledge team.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library lacks local or permit-specific rules for about half of the questions, so research (s2) keeps 88 (6.4); high: the library covers the rules as assumed and s2 keeps 75 (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track permit conditions and review dates, update plans and standard operating procedures, prepare permit applications from site data, have them approved, submit them and answer the authority's questions to obtain permits.

steps.what: Environmental engineer tracks permit conditions, expiry and review dates
Environmental engineer updates plans and standard operating procedures after changes
Environmental engineer checks the final plan or procedure before release: the change says what the site change and permit require, and it goes to the right site staff
Environmental engineer releases the checked plan or procedure version to site staff under document control
Environmental engineer prepares the permit application with site data
Site manager reviews the final permit application, its site data and reasoning, and approves it for submission to the authority
Environmental engineer submits the approved application through the government portal
Environmental engineer answers the authority's questions to obtain the permit

approvals.approved_version: The permit application with its site data and reasoning exactly as approved by the site manager in s4, submitted once through the government portal to the competent authority; any change goes back for a new approval.
The plan or procedure version exactly as checked by the engineer in s2b, released once under document control to the site staff who work to it; any change needs a new check and a new version.

tasks.design: Permits and their conditions sit in a compliance register with due dates and reminders instead of a spreadsheet. Plans and procedures are kept under document control with version history. Application forms fill site data such as volumes and emissions from the site's monitoring and production records, and the engineer writes the reasoning. The site manager approves before submission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Permit dates lived in spreadsheets and site data were copied into each application.
tasks.enabler_now: Compliance registers with reminders and forms filled from site records.
tasks.still_hard: Applications for new activities with no earlier data.
tasks.human_edge: Arguing an application in terms the authority accepts.
tasks.altitude: Fewer missed dates and less copying; writing and arguing stay.

reach.task: Run the site within its permit

evidence.claim: Cross-border hazardous waste procedures run electronically through an EU system since 21 May 2026.
Energy-saving information duty every four years; research duty from 10 million kWh per site.
Document control systems replace spreadsheets and e-mailed versions.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping permits and procedures current; the authority's decision is outside.
Input contract for s1: each permit's conditions and dates entered once by the engineer when granted.
Input contract for s3: volumes and emissions from the site's monitoring data and production records kept by site staff.

Submitting and answering questions keep their full time; the site manager's time is outside the engineer's savings. Updating plans and procedures keeps 90: document control removes keeping version lists and sending copies by hand, not the writing; checking and releasing each new version keep their full time.

incremental.description: Environmental engineer enters conditions of new or changed permits in the register.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: site records hold only half of the data the forms need, so preparing the application (s3) keeps 85 (17.4); high: forms fill volumes and emissions from site records as assumed (21.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan monitoring locations, direct installation of environmental monitoring devices, supervise data collection and data checks, arrange maintenance and calibration, and validate the dataset.

steps.what: Environmental engineer plans monitoring locations and devices
Environmental engineer directs installation of monitoring devices on site

Environmental engineer supervises data collection: gathers logger files and checks completeness and plausibility; after the change telemetry loggers send readings to the data platform and the engineer reviews the rule flags
Environmental engineer arranges maintenance and calibration with field technicians: from calibration reminders and data flags, with a work order prefilled with device and location
Environmental engineer checks the final work order: the device, location, fault or due calibration and the urgency match the flag or reminder, and it goes to the right technician team
Environmental engineer sends the checked work order to the field technicians
Field technicians enter the calibration date in the data platform after each calibration
Environmental engineer validates and signs off the monitoring dataset

tasks.design: Loggers with telemetry send readings to the data platform, where fixed rules flag gaps, flat lines, drift and values outside the device's range. The engineer looks at flags instead of opening every file. Calibration dates sit in the same platform and send reminders, and a flag can open a work order for the field technicians. Planning, installation and validating the dataset stay with the engineer.

approvals.approved_version: The work order with device, location, fault or due calibration and urgency exactly as checked by the engineer in s4b, sent once to the field technicians' queue in the data platform; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Logger files were downloaded on site visits and checked by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Telemetry loggers and data platforms with rule-based quality flags.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a real pollution event from a sensor fault.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the site well enough to read an odd value.

ambition.what: Check data quality daily instead of after each site visit.

tasks.altitude: Less file handling; judgement on data stays.

reach.learn: Whether flag-triggered visits fix faults sooner.

evidence.claim: Test data checks are dashboards and statistics; no model is needed.
AI used as a safety component in water, gas, heating or electricity supply is high-risk; quality flags on monitoring data are not.

assumptions: Boundary: from monitoring plan to validated dataset; reporting to the authority is outside.
Input contract for s3: loggers with telemetry installed by field technicians at about 70% of locations; the rest are downloaded on visits and loaded by hand; s3 is priced at that share.

Input contract for s4: calibration dates entered by the technicians after each calibration (s4d, share 1, replacing a mail to the engineer). Arranging keeps 70 because dates and prefilled orders remove looking up due dates and writing device details; checking and sending each work order keep their full time.
Planning, installation and validation keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of monitoring locations per engineer.
research_questions: Does data loss from faulty loggers fall?

already_counted.description: Environmental engineer reviews data quality flags.

incremental.description: Environmental engineer tunes flag thresholds per device type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: telemetry reaches only half of the locations, so data collection (s3) keeps 57 (16.1); high: telemetry at about 70% of locations as assumed (21.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
